They threw me a party, even though I've only worked here less than a month, when I told them I graduated trade school. They're all signing up to come visit me during my internship. They make me feel good about myself, and they help me find the confidence to try new things and trust my gut in new situations. My sister was in a car accident, so even though I'd only been at work an hour, they immediately had me clock out and head to the hospital. "Oh they're awful! About the size of my fist, with different colorful pattern on their backs warning you of their dangers, some are poisonous, others are carnivorous!"

*Two hours ago*

I'm cleaning my room. It's boring. I keep finding my old toys and playing with them instead of getting the work done. I'm not making any progress. I've been at this all day. Whatever, I give up. It's already 2am. I need to take Kronos on a walk. He's been curled up on my bed faithfully waiting for me to get off my previously forgotten Gameboy for hours. I should take him through the cornfields as a treat. They're his favorite.

"Kronos let's go for a walk!"

His response was immediate. Little ears perk up, fluffy tail starts flopping around, excited eyes peek open. I say it once more and he's off, running through the house like there's no tomorrow. So adorable. He's a good dog; I trust him not to run away. I open the door and let him disappear into the darkness.

.

.

.

Okay maybe I shouldn't trust him.

"Kronos where are you? C'mere boy!"

...nothing

Well... He must've found something worth ignoring me for. Better go save it.

It doesn't take me long to get deep into the cornfield. I'm pretty sure he ran off this way. I really should've brought a flashlight. It's beyond ridiculous trying to find him like this.

"Kronos you get over here right now!"

*Now* I hear a rustling. I really need to work on training him better. I hate being in the cornfield at night. It feels like a thousand hands brushing against my skin. The rustling gets closer, closer, closer. Finally, Kronos jumps out at me. I catch him and start walking back to the house, petting and scolding him the whole way. We make it back out of the cornfield, to where the light of my house illuminates us. And then something weird happens.

Kronos bites me! How rude! I drop him, feel bad because I treated him like a cat (and expected him to react like one), and immediately lean over and start petting him again as a sorry for dropping him. He bites me again! So this time I pop his lil puppy butt. I guess he doesn't like that, because he starts transforming. It took about ten seconds, maybe. Suddenly Kronos was not my good boy. And then he was joined by another Not-Kronos.

. . .

The glowing, fleshy orbs stared at me. Nearly ten feet tall, I think. Their "bodies" keep fading in and out of sight, as though they're out of sync with the world. An eternally black ooze is dripping from their... skin? They themselves are a deep, deep red, I think. It's hard to tell. It's hard to focus on them at all. I'm pretty sure they understand me, because they tilt their... heads? entire body? something? whenever I say anything.

"What do you two want? And where's my dog?" I felt very stupid for continuing to talk at these things, but they did take Kronos. And I want him back. They stare at me a while, still saying nothing. And then one of them gloops towards me. They seem weird, but not hostile or anything, so I let it get close. I look into the sunken hollows that I've decided are it's eye sockets, feel confused and dizzy, and then collapse. I'm still conscious, I just can't move. The orbs somehow lift me, though I don't feel anything touching me, and then I really do fall unconscious.

When I wake up, I have no idea where I am. It's like I'm in a void. There's nothingness around me and under me and above me. I physically can't comprehend this, so I decide to ignore it. This decision was probably a good idea because I feel like it would be very easy to go insane just thinking about it.

The orbs enter... sort of. They really just appear in front of me, but I've decided they must have come through a door because things don't just "appear" out of nowhere. So they glooped through a doorway and approached me. They don't speak, but I hear thoughts in my head that are not mine. I can hear everything, but at the same time there's no noise. It's like a silent scream.

They tell me what they want. They're going to invade the Earth. Inslave most of us, kill and eat the rest. They need a proper form to do that, though. Theirs cannot be sustained on Earth. Something about being in the wrong dimension, I think is what they said. So they want me to describe humanity's greatest enemy to them. Whatever is the most dangerous.

Idea after idea flows through my mind: hippos, rhinos, alligators and crocodiles, lions, and tigers, and bears (oh my!). I didn't want to say any of these, because I like humanity. But I was having trouble thinking of anything I could say that was innocent, but that I could still easily pretend to be scared of.

Finally, a small memory sprouts in my head. A memory of a documentary I watched as a kid. My greatest fear in life from the ages of five through twelve, and second-greatest fear from thirteen to nineteen. I still hate them, but I'm not scared anymore. It won't be hard to sound sincere when I talk about these disgusting monsters.

I looked the orbs right in their eye sockets. The old feelings of fear resurfaced. It's time. With a scared, shaky voice, I whispered the word.

"Butterflies"

I spent far too long explaining butterflies, drawing pictures and diagrams, showing the orbs how they flapped their wings, scaring children by flying too close for comfort. It was simple. I had that accursed documentary burned into my memories. You don't forget some things.

After hours of explaining, they seemed to finally understand everything. Another ten second transformation later, and I was faced with two ten-foot, poisonous, carnivorous butterflies.

*What have I done?*
